feedback: Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is a single-group test: sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016 at kp 7.0, kd 0.2, ki 0.0, with geometry positions, weights, base_speed 1.4 and line_loss last_direction unchanged. Each field is inside its contract range, and 0.016 is an allowed sensor_size. The earlier evidence supports the change. Iterations 0 to 4 all ended off_track with one line-loss event per run and max_error at 0.060 to 0.066 m, and kp alone moved progress (kp 6 gave oval 0.12, kp 7 gave 0.19, kp 8 gave 0.18). With 12 mm sensors at 0.02 m spacing and a 25 mm tape, a centre dead band is plausible, so this race tests it directly. Read the next race as follows. (a) If max_error falls below about 0.06 m and the s-bend progress rises above the flat 0.04 seen at kp 5 to 7, keep sensor_size 0.016 and reduce kp to 6.5 or widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.06 to cut steering_oscillation, which was 0.13 to 0.15 at kp 8. (b) If max_error and s-bend progress are unchanged, the stall is at a bend the sensors cannot follow, so test outer sensors at x = ±0.06 with sensor_size 0.016. (c) If the robot tracks without off_track but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed to 1.6 in a later single-group revision. Change one group per revision.
requested_changes: If max_error falls below about 0.06 m and s-bend progress rises above 0.04, keep sensor_size 0.016 and set kp to 6.5 with kd 0.2, since kp 8 raised steering_oscillation to 0.13 to 0.15 (iteration 2) while kp 6 gave oval progress only 0.12 (iteration 3).

If max_error and s-bend progress are unchanged with sensor_size 0.016, keep kp 7.0 and move the outer sensors to x = ±0.06 (positions at y 0.04), citing the flat s-bend progress of about 0.04 across kp 5, 6 and 7 (iterations 0, 3, 4).
If the robot tracks the line without off_track but completion_time exceeds 3 s, set base_speed = 1.6 in a single-group revision, since the 3.0 s limit needs an average speed of about 1.5 m/s.
